description: issue #864: the Core-only half of the Sprites value-position rule, and the byte-identical twin of `statement-heads-not-values`. `spec/turtles-and-sprites.md` gives `ask` and `each` a structural block-head role only while the Sprites profile is active -- it reserves the NAMES unconditionally (`spec/grammar.md:408`) -- so with Sprites inactive these are two names in value position that nothing in this program declares -- `ol-unknown-command` (`spec/tooling.md:181`), not the wrong-position `ol-bad-token` its twin reports for the very same bytes. The pair is what pins issue #864's rule as PROFILE-GATED rather than a blanket rejection: `ol-bad-token` is for a word the ACTIVE profile gives a structural role. Declaring one is a different question: a Core-only `define each ... end` raises `ol-reserved-word` (`spec/grammar.md:408`). `ask` carries `suggestion: "abs"`, which is the did-you-mean tie-break doing its ordinary job over the Core visible-name set -- primitives, special-form heads and declared names alike, not the primitive table alone (Levenshtein distance 2; candidate set and algorithm at `spec/error-model.md:195-208`); it is asserted rather than trimmed because a fixture must pin what the checker actually produces. This fixture asserts a NAME-visibility outcome, not a declaration one. This is a check-mode fixture: it proves static legality only and does not execute.
